description: Adopt Claude Code CLI tier aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku/default/...) as first-class model options plus a free-text passthrough, so new Anthropic models are picked up automatically with no dated-id drift.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Documented tier aliases for --model: default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan. Aliases point to the recommended version per provider and update over time; on the Anthropic subscription backend opus resolves to Opus 4.8 and sonnet to Sonnet 5. On Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry the same aliases resolve to different (often older) models, and full model names / dated ids pass through unresolved. Confirms the alias mechanism is the correct auto-tracking lever and that a pinned dated id (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) is the reproducible-snapshot escape hatch.

userStories.title: Adopt CLI tier aliases as the static model set (DEFAULTS + MODEL_OPTIONS + dogfood project.toml)
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need cam's built-in model set to be the Claude Code CLI tier aliases instead of dated snapshot ids, so a freshly-initialized project and cam's own loop auto-track the latest model of each tier with no stale list and no detection code.
acceptanceCriteria: DEFAULTS (src/config/models.ts) maps orchestrator/planner/auditor/reviewer to 'opus' and implementer/ship to 'sonnet' (tier aliases, no dated ids); backend stays 'claude'. [oracle: grep -Eq "implementer: 'sonnet'" src/config/models.ts]

MODEL_OPTIONS (src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx) offers the CLI tier aliases as first-class selectable entries: at minimum opus, sonnet, haiku, default, plus fable, opusplan, sonnet[1m], opus[1m]; each entry's description notes it auto-resolves to the current latest model of that tier, aligned with the Claude Code model-config docs. [oracle: grep -q "opusplan" src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx]

The alias-vs-dated trade-off is documented in the picker descriptions: aliases auto-track the latest of a tier (recommended, always-current), a dated id pins a reproducible snapshot, and 'default' is tier-aware (varies by subscription). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

readPhaseModel (src/config/models.ts) is confirmed to return any configured string verbatim with no allowlist rejection: a test asserts that a tier alias ('sonnet') and a custom dated id ('claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929') both flow through readPhaseModel unchanged (and are therefore passed as --model verbatim, the CLI validating at spawn). [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]
A test asserts the reconciled DEFAULTS are tier aliases (not dated ids) and resolve through the readPhaseModel -> --model path unchanged. [oracle: bun test test/config/models.test.ts]

The dogfood scripts/cam/project.toml [models] section uses tier aliases (no dated ids remain), removing the last in-repo dated-id drift site. [oracle: sh -c '! grep -Eq "claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-" scripts/cam/project.toml']

DEFAULTS-dependent tests are updated to the alias values so the suite is green (notably test/config/models.test.ts and test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx, which previously asserted claude-sonnet-5). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/config/models.ts (DEFAULTS map ~L51-59; readPhaseModel already returns verbatim at L82-97, no change to logic, just prove it), src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx (MODEL_OPTIONS ~L62-67), scripts/cam/project.toml ([models] section). Tests: test/config/models.test.ts, test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx. DEFAULTS is consumed by ConfigScreen's defaultValue={DEFAULTS[phase]} (L158) AND by cam init's scaffold (src/commands/setup.ts:700-707), so switching DEFAULTS to aliases makes fresh `cam init` projects auto-track automatically. This is why DEFAULTS + MODEL_OPTIONS must change together in one slice: Select.tsx computes initialIdx by finding defaultValue in options, so a DEFAULTS alias with a still-dated MODEL_OPTIONS would silently fall to index 0. Alias set MUST match the Claude Code model-config docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config): default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan. Gotchas: (a) cam is subscription-only via the claude CLI, do NOT add an Anthropic API-key path or a GET /v1/models poller, aliases ARE the mechanism; (b) aliases resolve only on Anthropic/subscription auth, on Bedrock/GCP/Azure the CLI passes strings through unresolved, so keep cam a pure --model passthrough and do not assume resolution for non-Anthropic readBackend; (c) many test files carry dated-id string fixtures (test/supervisor/*-argv-model.test.ts, test/commands/config-*.test.ts, test/commands/run-model-argv.test.ts) that assert verbatim passthrough of an explicit fixture value, those keep passing unchanged, only DEFAULTS-fallback assertions break. Do NOT touch vendor/ or templates/ (CAM-286 already stripped the inert frontmatter model: lines; ship's model source is cam-ship.md frontmatter, out of scope here). ADR-0034 already exists (docs/adr/0034-...md), do NOT recreate it; re-read it for the trade-off wording.

userStories.title: Add a free-text 'custom / enter id' passthrough to the config model picker
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need the config wizard to let me type an arbitrary model value so I can pin a specific dated snapshot (reproducible) or enter an unreleased/preview id that is not in the alias list, stored verbatim in project.toml.
acceptanceCriteria: The model-select step of the config wizard offers a 'custom / enter id' entry that, when chosen, reveals a free-text input (ink-text-input, mirroring SetupScreen's TextInput usage) for an arbitrary model value for that phase. [oracle: grep -q "ink-text-input" src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx]

A value typed into the custom input (e.g. a pinned dated snapshot 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929' or an unreleased id) is stored verbatim in ConfigChoices.models for that phase and written to scripts/cam/project.toml [models] unchanged, with no cam-side allowlist rejection. [oracle: bun test test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx]

Verify the screen renders correctly: an ink-testing-library test drives selecting the custom entry, typing a model id, confirming with Enter, and asserts the typed id appears in the step's confirmed summary; success/failure is signalled by the ✓/✗ glyph, never divider color. [oracle: bun test test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx]
Selecting a normal alias entry still advances the wizard as before (the custom path does not regress alias selection). [oracle: bun test test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: File: src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx (add a 'custom' sentinel entry to the per-phase model step and a TextInput sub-state that must be confirmed before the wizard advances to the next phase; handlePhaseSelect at ~L120 currently advances immediately, the custom path needs to defer setStepIdx until the id is entered). Reuse the TextInput pattern from src/ui/SetupScreen.tsx (import TextInput from 'ink-text-input', L39/L231; enter confirm / esc behaviour). Keep Select.tsx generic, handle the custom branch inside ConfigScreen rather than adding a text mode to Select. The write path already stores verbatim: mergeConfigChoices (src/commands/config.ts:115-119) writes choices.models as a TOML section and readPhaseModel returns it verbatim, so no config.ts change is needed, only the UI capture. Test: extend test/ui/config-screen.test.tsx (ink-testing-library, stdin.write for typing + '\r' to confirm; helpers test/helpers/flush-ink.ts waitForFrame and test/helpers/mock-terminal-size.ts installTerminalSizeMock are already imported there). Ink invariant: success is the ✓ glyph (ConfirmedChoice at L251), never divider color. Does NOT touch vendor/ or templates/, so no embed-vendor drift check. This story depends on US-001's alias MODEL_OPTIONS landing first (same file, avoids a same-file rebase and builds the custom entry alongside the alias list).
